text:
mike: Heads-up — updated spot forecast for next quarter shows a longer downside tail than our baseline. Running numbers for an "Effective Spot Yield" (ESY) metric and runway impact. Can FinOps weigh in?

finbot: Monthly spot exposure report ready: https://redwood.internal/reports/spot/2026-03. Uploaded sim outputs and raw traces.

sara: can you drop the assumptions? preemptible % by region, on-demand fallback cost, and SLA buffers.

mike: yep. assumptions in the snippet below — these are live-sim outputs for Mar->May. Please scan quickly.

mike: ```
Region   Preempt%  AvgInterruptRate  SpotPriceAvg  OnDemandUnit
us-west  72%       0.084             0.31          $3.20/hr
eu-west  65%       0.112             0.29          $3.40/hr
ap-south 40%       0.195             0.35          $3.90/hr
MixedPool effective_preempt=61% baseline_unit=$3.45
```

jia: propose ESY formula: `ESY = (effective_preempt * (on_demand_price - spot_price_avg) * (1 - interruption_loss_factor)) / on_demand_price` — it's the percent of on-demand cost we actually save after interruptions and ops overhead.

rahul: interruption_loss_factor we historically use 0.12 (12%) for ops + latency penalties on fallback. ok to keep?

sara: ok. if we adopt ESY for internal billing, we need smoothing to avoid whipsaw. recommend 3-month rolling ESY + a reserve buffer (default 20%) that we hold in a central pool. :bar_chart:

mike: quick calc from current sims => ESY_us-west ≈ 0.44, ESY_eu-west ≈ 0.38, ESY_ap-south ≈ 0.20 — so effective savings range 20–44% after accounting for interrupts.

jia: sounds right. also suggest capping ESY at 60% for chargeback math (we don't promise >60% realized savings).

rahul: ops note — preemptible pool us-west reported 88% utilization in the sim window, which increases risk of OOM/fallbacks. we should consider a small on-demand safety band.

ops-bot: alert: preemptible-pool-us-west utilization spike logged during sim run. More details: https://infra.internal/alerts/1779001111.

mike: thinking: add a configurable 5% on-demand safety band in high-util regions during peak windows to reduce interruption fallout. Rough trade: ~0.8% increase in baseline cost vs 3–4% reduction in fallback churn.

sara: for chargeback rule draft: `team_charge = base_on_demand_cost * (1 - ESY_adj) + tail_buffer_fee` where `ESY_adj = min(ESY_smoothed, 0.6)` and `tail_buffer_fee` is per-team depending on latency profile. We'll model 1/3/6 month smoothing.

jia: I'll produce a sample chargeback table showing per-team P&L under three scenarios (low/mid/high interruption) and include the tail buffer as a selectable option for product teams that need low-latency guarantees.

rahul: engineering action: if teams opt into "latency-protected" pool, infra will reserve on-demand capacity and pin critical pods. Otherwise they'll be billed with the ESY method and subject to higher variability.

mike: action items: (1) FinOps confirm ESY formula & smoothing param, (2) Product teams decide opt-in for latency-protected pools or accept ESY billing, (3) Infra to run 5% on-demand safety band test in us-west next Tue and return telemetry. I'll run sensitivity runs and upload them.

sara: ack. i'll model the P&L and add a recommended reserve size for the central buffer.

jia: will draft the chargeback spreadsheet and a one-pager explaining ESY and the tail buffer for the upcoming finance review.

mike: thanks :thumbsup: want decisions before Friday so next cycle invoicing can incorporate changes. cc @rahul.

finbot: sim bundle uploaded: /reports/spot/sim_runs/1779001111.zip — raw traces, cost matrices, and the scenario JSONs.

mike: closing the loop — i'll post the sensitivity output here once infra finishes the safety-band run.

sara: noted, ping me when results are in and i'll fold into the 3-month forecast.

jia: will also add a short note on how quantization/packing could change ESY assumptions long-term (small upside).

mike: great, thanks everyone.
